image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a sea lion resting on dark volcanic rock. The subject's head and upper torso are visible, showing wet, coarse fur with a mix of grey and brown tones. The eye is closed, suggesting sleep or rest. Prominent whiskers extend from the snout. A small external ear flap is visible behind the eye. Another sea lion's body is partially visible in the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head shape is visible, but the specific 'prominent sagittal crest' characteristic of mature males is not clearly defined or prominent in this angle/subject; the head appears relatively smooth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, small external ear flap is clearly visible on the side of the head, confirming it is an eared seal (sea lion/fur seal) and not a true seal.
Long, stiff whiskers are clearly visible extending from the muzzle area.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fur texture appears coarse and wet, with coloration matching the description (dark grey/brown). Ventral surface is not visible due to pose.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits streamlined fusiform form of substantial marine mammal proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows a thick, robust neck and torso consistent with a large marine mammal.
